name: Inwangsan Beombawi Course (Gyeongbokgung Stn → summit → Seochon)
desc: A course up via the Tiger Statue and Beombawi, B course down via the Forest Shelter and Choso Bookshop, then 4 restaurants at Sejong Village Food Street. From the video by 책쓰는 미식가.

line.name: Ascent: Gyeongbokgung Stn → Tiger Statue → Beombawi → summit (2.6 km, 1–1.5 h)

segments.label: Sajik-ro north sidewalk: Exit 1 → CU → Sajikdan gate
Along the Sajikdan stone wall, right onto Inwangsan-ro (Jarak-gil) → Tiger Statue
Stairs from the Tiger Statue up to the fortress wall (not mapped in OSM)
Beombawi → summit: granite cliff section, metal and stone stairs

pins.name: 1. Gyeongbokgung Stn Exit 1 – Start
pins.desc: Line 3. Walk west along Sajik-ro, the main road, towards the intersection. Station → summit takes about 1 h (1.5 h at a slow pace).

pins.name: 2. CU – last shop (buy 2 bottles of water)
pins.desc: Convenience store on the corner of the fork. There is not a single shop from here to the summit, so get at least 2 bottles of water. A sign at the fork points to another path; ignore it, cross the side road and pass the Sajikdan gate instead.

pins.name: 3. Sajikdan (Sajik Altar) gate
pins.desc: Pass the gate and follow the stone wall. At the end of the wall turn right: this is where Inwangsan Jarak-gil starts. Easy walking path, not a trail yet.

pins.name: 4. Ungyeong House (운경고택)
pins.desc: Joseon-era traditional house right after the corner, home of Ungyeong Lee Jae-hyung, a descendant of Prince Inseong. Opens only for occasional exhibitions. From here keep straight at every fork.

pins.name: 5. Hwanghakjeong archery pavilion
pins.desc: Tiled roof between the trees: an archery range built in 1898 under Emperor Gojong, with a free traditional archery museum. Looking is fine, photographing the archers is not. Just past it, next to the badminton club, is the LAST TOILET before the mountain.

pins.name: 6. Inwangsan Tiger Statue – trail entrance
pins.desc: Start of the Beombawi trail. 1.4 km / ~20 min from the station; a taxi to here saves that part. Turn LEFT at the statue into the trail entrance: steep stairs for 2–3 minutes, then the view opens and you are on the Hanyangdoseong fortress wall path. Beombawi is 800 m / ~20 min further. Illegal parking here is strictly enforced.

pins.name: 7. Viewpoint – fortress wall & Namsan Tower
pins.desc: Look back: the fortress wall and N Seoul Tower overlap here, with a small observation deck. The YouTuber's favourite angle, not too high. Over the wall to the left you can see Inwangsa temple and the oddly shaped Seonbawi rock, which Jeong Do-jeon deliberately left outside the wall.

pins.name: 8. Beombawi (Tiger Rock)
pins.desc: THE photo spot: the fortress wall winding towards Namsan Tower. Famous night-view point; many people climb only to here at sunset. Summit is 400 m further but it is the hardest part: slippery granite and a cliff section, hiking boots recommended. If you are already exhausted, turn back here. Expect a queue on weekends.

pins.name: 9. Inwangsan summit (338.2 m)
pins.desc: Panorama of Seoul: Namsan and N Seoul Tower, Lotte Tower, Jongno, Gwanghwamun and Gyeongbokgung; Bukhansan behind the Gichabawi ridge. The cliff below is Chimabawi (Skirt Rock), where deposed Queen Dangyeong spread her red skirt in 1506 to greet King Jungjong in the palace. Descent continues on the blue line.

line.name: Descent: summit → Forest Shelter → Choso Bookshop → Seochon (shortest way down)

segments.label: Summit → wall path north → Gichabawi junction
Follow the Changuimun sign along the wall → fork Suseongdong / Changuimun
B course: Suseongdong sign, past the Forest Shelter to the top of the boardwalk stairs
Steep boardwalk stairs down, cross Inwangsan-ro → Choso Bookshop
Inwangsan Jarak-gil down to Suseongdong Valley (650 m)
Through Seochon (Ogin-gil, Pirundae-ro, Jahamun-ro 9-gil) → Sejong Village Food Street

pins.name: 10. Gichabawi junction – check the signpost
pins.desc: First fork after the summit. Do NOT take the Gichabawi (Train Rock) direction: it leads to Hongje-dong, the opposite side from Seochon. Look for the Changuimun sign and go that way; Seochon should keep getting closer in the view.

pins.name: 11. Fork: Suseongdong Valley / Changuimun
pins.desc: The wall path splits. Straight on along the wall = C course to Changuimun in Buam-dong (facing Bukhansan and Bugaksan; stairs all the way; bus back to Gyeongbokgung Stn from the Yun Dong-ju Literature Museum). The Suseongdong Valley sign = B course, the shortest way down, followed here. The Forest Shelter is right next to this fork.

pins.name: 12. Inwangsan Forest Shelter (숲속쉼터)
pins.desc: Healing spot halfway down: a former military guard post turned into a free rest space open to everyone. Easy to miss, follow the sign and go inside. From here it is a short 300 m to Choso Bookshop: very steep but well-maintained stairs, no hiking boots needed.

pins.name: 13. Choso Bookshop (더숲 초소책방)
pins.desc: Old guard post rebuilt as a glass-walled café/bookshop that blends into the forest. You can end the hike here and call a taxi, or walk 650 m further down the Jarak-gil to Seochon. Also the starting point of the B course if you climb this way (village bus to Suseongdong Valley, then stairs only).

pins.name: 14. Suseongdong Valley bus stop
pins.desc: Village bus (Jongno 09) back to Gyeongbokgung Stn, or keep walking through Seochon to the food street.

pins.name: 15. Sejong Village Food Street – End (Exit 2)
pins.desc: Food alley starting at Gyeongbokgung Stn Exit 2, successor of the Geumcheongyo Market that existed since the Goryeo era; officially designated in 2011. The 4 restaurants from the video are in the Restaurants layer.

pins.name: Seochon Gyedanjip (서촌 계단집) – seasonal seafood
pins.desc: Old-school seafood joint featured on 'Wednesday Food Talk'; sells the season, so the menu changes with the catch and the cooking stays simple. Basic set: mussel soup, carrot, onion, ssamjang. Autumn: bone-in gizzard shad sashimi; wild rock oysters; cuttlefish blanched or steamed; steamed blue crab; order raw shrimp whenever it is on the menu. The kick: finish with 'bada-ramyeon', ramyeon boiled with the shrimp heads and seasonal shellfish, soup like a haemultang. Two rooms across a narrow alley, you fetch drinks from the fridge yourself.

pins.name: Naejadong Chuncheon Dakgalbi (내자동 닭갈비)
pins.desc: Pleasantly spicy charcoal dakgalbi, not too strong, no queue, relaxed and spacious; a good alternative when the hot spots are overrun with tourists. Fry the marinated chicken on the hotplate, then the highlight: the fried rice at the end. Sides: rice balls you roll yourself with seaweed flakes, and soft steamed egg to balance the heat.

pins.name: Kimjin Moksam main branch (김진목삼 본점) – thick samgyeopsal
pins.desc: Popular pork belly place run by the son of a 30-year butcher's; home-grown vegetables and house-made kimchi from Korean ingredients. Staff grill the meat for you and check the plate temperature. Dip the pork in myeoljeot (fermented anchovy sauce). A bit pricey, register for the waiting list on your phone and expect a long wait; not a place to linger.

pins.name: Mokpo Sebal Nakji (목포세발낙지) – spicy stir-fried octopus
pins.desc: 1 minute on foot from Kimjin Moksam, on Pirundae-ro just outside the busy market alley. Fresh live octopus; the nakji-bokkeum is cooked to the right point in the kitchen first so it arrives soft and springy, with a proper smoky fire taste. Moved a few doors a few years ago, same quality.
